about: Where this SDK, replaying a shared recording from rius-semconv, produces something other than the recording's stored expected result. For the families both SDKs cover the expected result is the Python SDK's, so these are the places the two SDKs disagree. Each entry is reviewed and says why. tests/conformance.test.ts fails on any difference not listed here and on a listed one that no longer occurs, so fixing a difference means deleting its entry in the same change. `key` is an attribute key, or one of `events`, `status`, `name`, `kind`; "*" covers every difference in the family. `awaiting_expected` lists recorded scenarios whose reference expected result does not exist yet; the test skips them, and fails once one exists, so its entry is deleted in the change that syncs it.

differences.reason: LiteLLM is Python-only, so this SDK never sees these spans live and does not move a LiteLLM wrapper's usage. The Python SDK, the reference here, moves the completion span's usage to rius.aggregated_usage.* when its OpenAI child recorded the same call.

This SDK maps OpenInference's audio token details to the audio usage subsets, as rius-semconv's media parts change decides; the Python SDK, whose output is this family's expected result, makes the same change in its own media parts work, and the regenerated expected result retires this entry. The registry's usage_keys.yaml still says ignored until then.
